what_it_does: When you use fully homomorphic encryption (FHE)—a technique that lets you run calculations on encrypted data without decrypting it—repeated multiplications cause the encrypted data to grow and exhaust its computational 'capacity,' requiring expensive restoration steps called bootstrapping. This paper describes ReSBM, a compiler tool that automatically figures out where to place the fewest bootstrapping operations needed during an encrypted machine-learning inference (the actual computation using an AI model). It uses a graph-cut algorithm to partition the calculation into regions and insert bootstrapping only where necessary, reducing overall computational overhead while keeping the encryption secure.
